```{r}
library(car)
library(GGally)
library(performance)
library(infer)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
df_WtDo <- read_csv("Santori_Wt_Change.csv")

df_WtDo %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = MID)) +
  geom_histogram()

df_WtDo %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Before)) +
  geom_histogram()

df_WtDo %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = After)) +
  geom_histogram()

df_WtDo %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Wt_change)) +
  geom_histogram()






```

```{r}
# Calculate After - Before - Wt_change
difference <- with(df_WtDo, After - Before - Wt_change)

# Plot a histogram
hist(difference,
     main = "Check of recorded weight change",
     xlab = "After - Before - Wt_change",
     col = "lightblue",
     breaks = 30)

```


```{r}
  # before weight= 100kg, after weight =10kg, wt_change=50 kg
# 50-100+10= 60

df_WtDo %>%
  group_by(Diet) %>%
  summarise(N = n())

df_WtDo_lo_hi<- df_WtDo %>%
  filter(Diet %in% c(36,84))

# Q2. What kind of plot would best illustrate the pattern?
# a box pllot would be awsome, but we are not gonna do that

#Q3. What are your guesses for the mean values (in a notebook or in annotations) for each level of the predictor?
# I reccon the higher grade of food the higher the weight gain

lm_wt_change_2level <- lm(Wt_change ~ factor(Diet),
                          data = df_WtDo_lo_hi)

check_model(lm_wt_change_2level)


df_WtDo_lo_hi %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Diet, y = Wt_change)) +
  geom_point()


lm_wt_change_cont <- lm(Wt_change ~ factor(Diet),
                          data = df_WtDo)


check_model(lm_wt_change_cont)


df_WtDo %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x = Diet, y = Wt_change)) +
  geom_point()

mod1 <- aov(Wt_change ~ factor(Diet), data = df_WtDo)

summary(mod1)

mod2 <- aov(Wt_change ~ factor(Diet), data = df_WtDo_lo_hi)

summary(mod2)

# Q5: What does the suffix (number 84) mean in the table of coefficients?
# diet "score 84"

# Q6. Why doesn’t the model just estimate the intercept for each group as a deviation from the global mean, instead of estimating a reference intercept and deviations?
# 

summary(lm_wt_change_cont)


t.test(Wt_change ~ Diet,
       data=df_WtDo_lo_hi)


df_WtDo_lo_hi %>%
  t_test(Wt_change ~ Diet)


aov_wt_change_2level <- aov(Wt_change ~ Diet,
                            data=df_WtDo_lo_hi)


summary(aov_wt_change_2level)


```

```{r}
lm_wt_change_5level <- lm(Wt_change ~ factor(Diet), data = df_WtDo)

check_model(lm_wt_change_5level)

summary(lm_wt_change_5level)

df_Santori_fac <- df_WtDo %>%
  
  mutate(Diet_fac = factor(Diet)) %>% 
  
  mutate(Diet_fac = fct_relevel(Diet_fac, "60"))

```

check if this worked  vv

```{r}
levels(df_Santori_fac$Diet_fac)



lm_wt_change_5level_60ref <- lm(Wt_change ~ Diet_fac,
                                
                                data = df_Santori_fac) 

summary(lm_wt_change_5level_60ref)


lm_wt_change_5level <- lm(Wt_change ~ factor(Diet), data = df_WtDo)

check_model(lm_wt_change_5level)
summary(lm_wt_change_5level)

df_Santori_fac <- df_WtDo %>%
  mutate(Diet_fac = factor(Diet)) %>% 
  mutate(Diet_fac = fct_relevel(Diet_fac, "60"))
# check that this worked
levels(df_Santori_fac$Diet_fac)

lm_wt_change_5level_60ref <- lm(Wt_change ~ Diet_fac,
                                data = df_Santori_fac) 
summary(lm_wt_change_5level_60ref)

df_new_wt_change <-
  crossing(Diet = c(36,48,60,72,84))

preds <- predict(lm_wt_change_5level, 
                 newdata = df_new_wt_change,
                 int = "c")

df_preds <- bind_cols(df_new_wt_change, as_tibble(preds))
df_preds %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Diet, y = fit)) +
  geom_jitter(data = df_WtDo, aes(y = Wt_change),
 alpha = 0.3, height = 0, width = 1) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(y = fit,
                      ymin = lwr,
                      ymax = upr),
                  colour = "red",
                  size = 1.2) + labs(y = "Weight change (g)",
                                     x = "Diet (% nutrition)")  

```
